Before we flew, Bruce clarified the traffic patterns unique to the Island. We then did 1. familiarization / training session and 2. a photography session, both over 1 hour long. We did not want the flights to end.

Bruce kindly let me (the pilot) fly out of the left seat and guided me around the island traffic pattern, while we flew around the coast, the canyon and the mountains. Bruce pointed out interesting landmarks and locations where famous movies have been shot. We chatted about various issues related to mountain flying, strategies for monitoring traffic and bird avoidance.

In the second flight Bruce kindly let us open the right window to get clear photo shots, free of reflections and distortions. He positioned the aircraft at an appropriate distance, and considered the direction of light for good shot opportunities. It is clear that he understands the needs of a photographer. He encouraged me to take control from the right seat (with which I did not have much experience) and all worked out well.

Bruce is an excellent pilot and an excellent instructor and quickly finds the level at which his student functions, communicates and encourages at an appropriate level. Ellen runs the office professionally and in a personally attuned way. All aspects of the experience have been pleasant. We look forward to more flying with Wings Over Kauai in the future and highly recommend the experience as safe, educational and adaptive to individual likes, needs and skill levels (pilots).

Michael Krelina, M.D., Jane Barlow, M.D.
Canada

Everyone agreed this was the best tour we could have possibly done.  We always try to book privately and not through the cruiseline.  It helps the independent small business owner.  This company goes above and beyond when it comes to customer service.  We will definitely do this tour again when we return to Kauai.  If you cruise on Norwegian's Pride of America, rent a car the first day in port and drive the island. (We started driving at 8:30 a.m. and returned the car at 8:00 p.m. and saw the entire island.) Review Text:
I am a very bad flier. Very nervous, can't handle turbulence, etc. So when my husband asked if I wanted to go on a flight on a very small plane through Wings Over Kauai I wasn't exactly sold...

Having now done it (and survived!!) all I can say is, wow. This is such an amazing experience and I'm so happy we chose Wings Over Kauai.

Booking a flight was easy and Ellen responded quickly to all of our emails. She also sent perfect directions so we arrived at the terminal and parked with no issues.

When we arrived Ellen prepped us for the flight by giving us some tips and asking if we have issues with motion sickness (I do), then she gave me a beautiful kukui nut lei and took a picture of us in front of the plane.

She helped me get situated in the front of the plane and gave me peppermint and ginger chews to help with motion sickness. They also have small bottles of water on the plane.

Bruce was our pilot and he was amazing. He's very calm and knows absolutely everything about Kauai so kept up a soothing commentary throughout the flight. I had a bit of a death grip on my chair every time we hit a bump in the air but as Bruce was so calm and in control it really helped me enjoy the flight much more than I thought possible. Takeoff and landing were very smooth and we were lucky to have a pretty smooth flight. The views are stunning and you get to see parts of the island you'd never easily be able to access otherwise, this is a must do on Kauai!

Review Text:

Don't forget to bring the camera because the views from above are gorgeous. In retrospect, I think that it should have been the first thing that we should have done because Bruce is very knowledgeable about the island and not averse to a lot of questions. In fact he welcomes them and keeps checking in on you throughout the flight. By the end of the tour, you are able to plan your itinerary and know about the spots to hit according to your time on the island.

When you check in, Ellen is a great host and very personable. She followed up with us with a couple of photos through email and even gave us separate DVDs of the beautiful video shot by their son who is an aspiring cinematographer in Hollywood. My only suggestion would be to upgrade it to HD video.

Great people, great tour, great island. Thanks Ellen and Bruce. Don't do air or water, do both, especially, for Na Pali. I am still not done with Kauai.

Review Text: As an American living in Japan, flight training is difficult to get because it's expensive...and in Japanese. As such, both of my two training flights (so far) were done on vacation, first in Guam, then here at Wings Over Kaua'i. I have to say, Wings Over Kaua'i was at least 10 times better-- no exaggeration. The instructor worked with me and my specific needs-- NOT another island tour, but actual flight training. We went over to Port Allen, an uncontrolled field just SW of Lihu'e and practiced 2 touch-and-go's, went over the sea and practiced climbs, descents, stalls, and steep turns (my personal favorite). When we got back to the office, the people there were friendly and just as excited as I was -- you can tell they love their jobs. They even gave us a complimentary CD of our flight! Additionally, the CFI there was very helpful when I asked him about the right way to approach my training, and I ended up buying the FAA-authored Airplane Flying Handbook for just $20 -- only $2 over what the retail price was. All in all, an amazing experience...I'm looking forward to this Tuesday!

Review Text:
These guys earned their 5 stars from the time of booking to the moment we returned to our car.

It was good to deal with a family run business and they certainly lived up to the high expectations that we had built up from all the TripAdvisor reviews.

The booking process with Ellen was efficient and really friendly. We're from the UK, with an 11 hour time difference, so everything was organised on line and by email. Responses came back by return, and provided all the information we needed. We booked our flight and were not even asked for a deposit. Ellen's response when we offered a payment was "we are just using the honor system to hold reservations and it seems to be working really well". A nice touch.

Our weather in Kauai was great but with some seriously strong winds and we were a little nervous about going up in a small 4 seater Cessner. Upon arrival at their office they assured us it would be ok, although they did warn us that there would be a few bumps! Before completing the paperwork and taking our money they suggested we speak with the passengers who were coming back from the previous flight. They offered to cancel the booking or re-arrange it for another day if we were concerned. There was no pressure on us whatsoever to fly, which we really appreciated. We eventually decided to go for it and are so glad we did.

Carter (Ellen and Bruce's son) looked after us while we were waiting, and was great. He then introduced us to Bruce, our pilot. Bruce's style is incredibly calming and he gave an excellent commentary on the landscape, history, flora and fauna, whilst chatting with us throughout the flight. He is not a typical tour guide, he is genuinely knowledgeable and interesting and clearly loves the island. The flight was amazing and we saw virtually everything. Kauai is absolutely stunning from the air.

After an extremely smooth landing, we went back into the office and were presented with a "home made" but good quality DVD of a typical flight, personalised with our photos, which had been taken as we boarded the plane. The photos were later emailed to us.

Having flown over Maui in a Blue Hawaiian helicopter a few years ago and been stuck in the middle seat, with limited visibility, I loved the fact that "Wings" only use the right hand seats of their aircraft to give everyone the best view. Also, the safety record of tour helicopters in Hawaii is not great and following the sad Blue Hawaiian crash on Kauai at the end of 2011, we felt a lot safer opting for a fixed wing plane.

A plane can't get into the valleys in quite the same way as a helicopter, but I remember from the previous flight that we spent a lot of time hovering and circling around so that everyone could get a view. With the fixed wing flight, it felt that we were getting a much better overview of the whole island, and at only 1,500 feet, the scenery still felt very close. It was just as good, if not better, than a helicopter.

We chose to fly with Wings primarily because of the safety issues and the seating arrangements. It was not really a cost based decision but, at about half the price of a helicopter flight, we thought it was amazing value for money.

Finally, having landed and been given our DVD, we walked back to our car and as we were getting in, Bruce made the effort to come over to offer directions and suggestions for the rest of the day.

We loved the personal and genuinely friendly service of Wings over Kauai and their professionalism throughout and recommend them one hundred percent.

Review Text:
When my husband and I visited Kauai in June 2012, the winds were unseasonably strong. With my sea sickness, a catamaran to see the Napali Coastline, as we had originally planned, was out of the question. When we discovered how expensive a helicopter tour was, I was devastated because seeing Kauai has been on my bucket list. The concierge at our hotel recommended Wings Over Kauai because it was half the cost of a helicopter and wouldn't contribute to motion sickness like a catamaran would. It was the perfect suggestion!

We had a 2:30 take off time. I was given a kukui shell necklace and Bruce, the pilot/owner, took a photo of my husband and I in front of the plane before we took off. He had me sit up front in the cockpit with him because I'm prone to motion sickness, and he gave a bunch of tips to help me deal with any sickness I might feel. They had water on board for us, and the tour was extremely informative, as Bruce is a retired agronomist who used to work on hybrid corn and soybeans on Kauai. Not only was there history involved in the commentary he provided, but there was also a lot of interesting geological information that I don't think any other experience could have provided.

The tour lasted an hour and went around the island, getting to see all the highlights. Bruce was an awesome tour guide and pilot, and even told us facts about the plane. Once we landed (very, very smooth landing), we were given a CD with our photo on it that is almost like a promotion DVD of Wings Over Kauai set to Hawaiian music. It's not informative, but you get to see all of the beautiful scenery again, and it was a perfect souvenir!

I would definitely recommend Wings Over Kauai to others visiting Kauai, especially if you have motion sickness or if seeing Kauai by foot or sea is not an option!

Review Text:
We did a helicopter tour 20 years ago which I can barely remember since I was in the middle of the back so I couldn't really see anything. When I looked up helicopter tours this trip, the seating showed that only 3 of the 6 passengers would have be next to a window. Since the price is the same no matter where you sit and the seating is based on weight distribution, it didn't seem worth the risk to pay so much for a high probability of poor viewing.

The helicopter tours run 1.5-2 times the cost for a slightly shorter ride time. We chose Wings and are very glad we did. We checked in with Bruce and Ellen's daughter who was very pleasant and informative. We were in the Cessna with Bruce, the owner/pilot. My teen daughter gets motion-sickness so he recommended she sit up front. There was a cooler with waters, mints and ginger candies an He immediately engaged her as "co-pilot" - reading off his safety checklist. He took the time to explain each item - what it was for, etc, which was both interesting and reassuring. He gave my daughter, an avid photographer, some suggestions on how to get good pix and how to minimize motion-sickness. As we waited for clearance to take-off, Bruce explained about runway markings and other plane info. He also teaches flying and I think he'd be great - very calm and patient.

Bruce is a PhD agronomist and was full of information on the island from scientific to movie/tv locations and celebrity visits, to living and raising a family on Kauai. We each had headphones with microphones, so we could all talk to each other, ask questions, etc. He tailored the trip to avoid more turbulent areas and let my daughter know when it would be bumpy and when it would smooth out.

When we landed his daughter presented us with a dvd that had our picture on the front - a nice touch. I recommend this tour whole-heartedly.

Review Title: Fun Viewing Kauai from the air
Review Text:
We enjoyed our air tour of Kauai flying Wings Over Kauai in their six seater fixed-wing aircraft. Wings Over guarantees a window seat on the right side of the plane for every customer. This is crucial to getting a great view of the island from the air and getting your money's worth.

Bruce Coulombe, the owner/pilot, is a retired scientist and very knowledgeable. We thoroughly enjoyed his commentary and insights as we flew. Bruce is a veteran pilot with more than 5,000 flights over Kauai.

One drawback of the fixed wing aircraft is that it cannot get up close to many of the waterfalls and ridges that a helicopter can. For us, this was for the best because one of our party members tends to get motion sickness. Bruce and Ellen also made sure that the person with the tendency for motion sickness got to sit in the co-pilot seat to minimize the effects of the motion of the plane.

Review Text:
Ellen, Bruce and Joshua are a great team and make their customers feel welcome and relaxed. I had come to Kauai specifically to see the Na Pali coast by air (since i could no longer hike it). The fixed wing plane was good value and Bruce was a fount of information. The fixed winged plane does not go into the canyons but looking at helicopters that did, I was glad that the plane did not do that - a sudden gust of wind could be extremely dangerous.
Kauai is beautiful from the air and with so many contrasts it is a delight to see. We had seen the Waimea Canyon from the road the previous day and the plane view gave a wonderfully different perspective. Flying over Princeville and the northern coast was also lovely and gave us an idea of whether we wanted to visit there or not. If you are a golfer then there are some very interesting and beautiful golf courses.
Be ready with your camera and dont lean it against the window - it damages the windows. The opportunities for photographs are quick so you really need to be prepared. Video of the trip would be great. Bruce's son has produced a CD with photographs taken of customers before the trip and highlights of what is seen on a typical trip. A great souvenir. They also present the women passengers with a Kuki nut lei.
Bruce was an agronomist and is able to tell you all about the crops and flora of the island. The forest of abiza trees from Africa are beautiful - hopefully they are not an invasive pest.
We were lucky enough to see some waterfalls as there had been a lot of rain recently. The extinct volcano in the middle of the island has the highest record of rainfall in comparison with other parts of Kauai so there were quite a few waterfalls on he northern side.
Ellen provides air sickness ginger candy for those with queezy stomachs and cold drinks in the form of cola and water. Bruce goes through all the safety checks before take off including the use of life jackets.
The plane we flew had been made in Gippsland (Australia) and took six passengers as well as the pilot. It was comfortable. Note that the seating of passengers take place according to weight so you may not get the seat you had hoped for. However all seats have good views and Bruce will point out places and things of interest if you advise him before hand of your particular interests.
The fixed plane cost is roughly half the cost of a helicopter flight. It is good value indeed.
The waiting area looks over the helicopter landing area and you can sit in the open air and watch the helicopters taking off.
This was an event to remember and we will certainly be talking about for a long time to come.

Review Title: Best way to see all of Kauai
Review Text:

The plane tour is half the price of a helicopter tour and covers the same area, but is slightly longer than the helicopter tour (about 70 minutes versus 55-60 with a helicopter). The helicopters will take you closer to waterfalls and such, but I kind of liked seeing them from a longer distance as you get a better perspective of the area.

Definitely worth the money. At the end you also get a surprise gift - but I won't spoil the surprise by telling you what it is. Patience, people, patience!

Review Text: I decided to go with Wings Over Kauai due to the "Mom and Pop" feel of the company.  It was one of the best decisions I made about our Kauai trip.  Ellen was extremely kind in both booking the tour and when we arrived.  She sent out a confirmation e-mail that you could tell she wrote and wasn't one they just change the names on and send to everyone.  While waiting for the tour, Bruce came out for a little chit chat with the wife and I.  He didn't have to do this but it showed they care about the people they take up.  Their son gave us the safety briefing and was also very friendly.  The weather had been bad for a couple days and the pilot Paul was honest about what we may or may not see.  I decided I would rather see half of something than nothing at all.  Ellen came along on our tour to help narrate and I'm glad she did.  Most of the island was clear and we could see a lot.  When we got to the Na Pali coast the weather there wasn't favorable so we had to stay a decent distance from the cliffs for safety.  In doing so I was able to spot a few whales right below us and the pilot took the time to do a few circles so we could all get a great view.  Both Ellen and Paul did great at narrating and Paul was quite hilarious.  It honestly didn't feel like a tour at all.  It felt as if some friends took us up in their plane to show us around the island.  It was one of our most memorable experiences from our trip.  I took the 9:30AM tour and when we landed I wanted to get back on for the 11:00AM tour but my wife was hungry.  After eating and heading back to Poipu my wife called to see if we could get an afternoon tour but the weather had turned bad and they said they weren't going up again that day.  We loved it so much we wanted to go back up the same day.  We had other tours booked for the rest of our stay so unfortunately we weren't able to go up a second time.  I highly recommend this to anyone thinking about an air tour of Kauai.  The island is best seen from the air due to the topography.  I will definitely fly with them again on my return to Kauai.

Review Text:
Wir wurden sehr freundlich begrüßt und ich bekam eine Kette aus... , ja, was sind das eigentlich für schwarze, grau gemaserte Steine? Ich habe keine Ahnung, trotzdem eine sehr nette Willkommensgeste. Außerdem noch eine frische Blüte, die leider nicht in meinem Haar hält.
Auch hier wurden wir wieder gewogen- wir waren aber die einzigen Passagiere für diesen Flug. „Wings over Kauai“ hat zwei Flugzeuge, ein etwas größeres, einen Gippsland GA-8 Air Van für 6 Passagiere und eine Cessna Skyhawk 172 für 2 bis 3 Mitflieger. Karl-Heinz durfte in der Cessna vorn neben dem Piloten Platz nehmen- er wurde dabei ganz schnell mal zum Co Piloten befördert und arbeitete gleich die Checkliste vor dem Start mit ab. Dazu bekam er ein kleines Kunststoffbord auf dem alle zu prüfenden Dinge draufstehen- wenn der Pilot sein o. k. gab, wurde ein Stift an der Seite neben der Frage reingeschoben. Waren alle Details mit „ja“ beantwortet, ergab das eine glatte Linie und wir konnten ruhig starten.
Bruce- unser Pilot- erklärte und zeigte uns die Schönheiten Kauai`s aus der Vogelperspektive. Jurassic Park, James Bond`s „Goldfinger“, The Decenders und vielen anderen Filmen diente die Insel schon als Kulisse.
Die Wasserfälle, die wir uns am Vormittag angesehen hatten, sahen aus der Luft viel gewaltiger und schöner aus. Auch unsere künftigen Wanderwege konnten wir schon mal aus der Höhe betrachten und auf Tauglichkeit untersuchen.
Nochmals herzlichen Dank an Bruce, es war fast wie zu Hause mit Volker fliegen- nur die Gegend war einfach spektakulärer. Zum Abschluß gab es für uns noch eine DVD vom Rundflug. Danke.
Zu erwähnen wäre noch, dass wir uns absolut sicher fühlten. Bruce ist schon mehr als 5000 Mal um die Insel geflogen. Es gab vor dem Flug eine ordentliche Sicherheitseinweisung.
Die Maschine verfügte über hochwertige Bose Kopfhörer die irgendwie die Triebwerksgeräusche wegfilterten.
Ein sehr schönes individuelles Erlebnis ohne die bei Hubschrauberflügen übliche Massenabfertigung und außerdem noch preiswerter

Review Text:
Visitors cannot grasp the full beauty of Kaua'i without an aerial tour. If your budget, health, and stomach are not obstacles, go with the helicopter tour. If you are nervous about flying in a small plane or are prone to motion sickness Wings Over Kauai is a perfect choice. Ellen and Bruce own this small business and understand that people need reassurance for air travel in a plane that seems so small and fragile. You can trust that Bruce will not fly if conditions are not right and he will get you off and back safe and sound. Ellen provides ginger candies that really help with queasiness.
Our preference was to take the helicopter flight but our budget is limited and we found this tour the best choice. The competitor was doing a brisk business, but I know ours was a superior trip because of the accurate description of everything we saw by Bruce who is very knowledgeable. Because we chose the airplane trip instead of the helicopter, we were able to afford a boat cruise with Holo-holo that gave us an up close vantage of the Naal Pali coast. In addition, we rented a car and drove around to see all the views from ground level.
One of the other reviewers noted a delay in starting due to flooding the engine on take off. This happened at the start of our flight, too--and it was nerve wracking. However, Bruce is calm and reassuring so we didn't feel uneasy about possible problems while in flight.
I had a seat to the left and missed many sights but had a beautifull view of the ocean and saw a whale during the flight.

Review Title: Not as good when it's Bruce's day off
Review Text: My husband and I visited Kauai in February 2012 with out toddler son and my parents. While there, my parents wanted to do something adventurous and saw Wings Over Kauai was the top attraction on TripAdvisor. My father called to see if any time was available during our last few days on the island and he was able to book a time for himself and my mother to go the next day. They went on the tour and came back to our hotel and just raved about the experience! They had a blast and thought that Capt. Bruce was wonderful and everyone there was so nice. They had such a good time that, even though I was scared to fly in a small plane, talked my husband and I into calling to see if there was any other times available for us to go. There was an opening two days later they were able to fit us in and while excited to go, I was very nervous too. Our flight time arrived and my parents dropped us off at the airport. I was still very nervous about the flight. Carter greeted us and checked us in, he was very nice. The flight before ours arrived back and my father quickly noticed it was not Bruce flying. Carter mentioned it was Bruce's day off. We were sad we didn't get to meet Bruce, whom my parents just raved about, but figured it would still be great. After checking in, we watched out the window as the pilot messed around with the plane hood up. It was not comforting to see that. Then we were taken out to the plane and seated. We met the substitute pilot (and now I can't even recall his name because I was too nervous) and got settled in the plane. The pilot then tried to start the plane and it wouldn't start. Now, I know nothing about planes so as a clueless passenger when a plane won't start, it is a little nerve-wracking. The pilot would try to start it and then we would have to wait about 5 mins and then he would try again. This went on for about 5 times and it finally started on what he said was his final try. I was about ready to demand to get off the plane when it started. And I noticed my parents and son looking out the window in concern as well when were weren't moving. Then I questioned the reliability of the plane for our flight and was basically laughed at by the pilot and another passenger. The flight itself was just OK. The pilot talked a bit about the sights below but really didn't have a conversation with us like my parents (and all the other TripAdvisor reviewers) said Bruce did. He knew I was clearly nervous but did nothing to make sure we felt relaxed. The views were beautiful and it was a nice time but I don't think it was even close to the same experience my parents had. The pilot was friendly but just didn't make it amazing like others mention when they talk about going with Bruce. I would recommend this tour to others but  would say to make sure Bruce isn't off the day they go. I completely understand that he needs a day off, just like everyone else, but they may need to teach the substitute pilot to offer a similar experience to the one Bruce gives. It was just night and day differences between two different tours in two days. I am still giving this a Very Good rating because I know how good it was for my parents and do think it was worth doing.

Review Title: Beautiful, Fun, Tour of the Island!
Review Text:
After reading so many positive reviews of this tour and the experience, we decided to give this a try since I am a little prone to motion sickness and I was a little scared to do the helicopter tour. Great experience from beginning to end. Made reservations with Ellen, who was very friendly and even offered advice on what day to try and book because of the weather being rainy on some days. It was sunny but a little windy on the morning of our tour, and Ellen called us that morning to let us know of the wind factor and gave us the opportunity to reschedule. I appreciated her honesty and the warning. In the end, she said to come on in and we could get an idea of how windy the tour was from the earlier tour that went before us. We checked in with Bruce and Ellen, and everything was easy and fast. They even gave us reading material on the island while we waited. I especially enjoyed the book about movies filmed on Kauai. Bruce and Ellen run this great family-run business and they do everything right, right down to making everything feel personal. Ellen even offered us all some ginger candy before the flight to help with any motion sickness.

We decided to go ahead with the tour, and flew with Pilot Shane, who was fun, energetic, and very informative. Despite the wind, the flight was very comfortable, allowed us to all see a great view of the island. Everyone gets a window seat so everyone gets a great view of the island to take pictures & video. We all got a microphoned headset so we can communicate with each other during the tour. Overall a great experience and a MUST DO on your trip to Kauai. Mahalo to Bruce, Ellen, and Shane for making us feel so welcome and for a great time!

Review Title: great way to tour the island
Review Text:
my wife and i originally planned on taking a heli tour on our honeymoon, but there are three things that turned me off from the helis:

1. the cost (much more expensive than this plane tour)
2. assigned seating in heli's based upon weight and the possibility that you could be seated in the middle of the heli with a terrible view, but you'd still have to pay full price.
3. i'm a bit weary of helicopter safety. they just seem to be unsafe in my opinion and coincidentally there was a tragic crash in maui several days ago.

all that being said, everything about the tour was great. ellen who is the travel coordinator was very helpful with booking the tour and graciously answering questions i had about things to do in kauai. the plane was piloted by captain shane who is putting in his hours on his way to hawaiin airlines. he's very knowledgeable about the island and gives a very laid back tour of the island.

my expectations were that we would fly way to fast past all the sights on the island because we were in a plane, but that was not the case. in fact there were times that we did a 360 loop so that we could survey certain areas for longer periods of time. good stuff.

the only minor complaint i have is that because you're in a plane, your pictures have to be taken beyond the glass. depending on the conditions, the sun can create a lot of glare against the glass. i didn't mind too much though, because honestly our camera wasn't high quality enough to really capture the beauty of what we say anyway.

Review Title: The Highlight of our Hawaiian Vacation
Review Text:
What can I say that hasn't already been said? Fabulous! Breathtaking! Wonderful!
After reading the reviews on Trip Advisor, I decided to look no more. Wings over Kauai was an excellent decision; always to be remembered.
We were picked up near our cruise ship and brought to the airport (no extra charge). Bruce and Ellen provided a very, personal experience by making us welcomed. Ellen by making us feel like old friends and easing my fears and Bruce by addressing each one of us during the flight by name and sharing personal experiences. We were offered a delicious Hawaiian pastry & I was presented with a Kukui nut lei, & native flower (no extra charge). We were assured a fantastic experience and that it was.

We were able to communicate to each other through a state-of-the-art headphone system. Noise and vibration was almost non-existent in comparison to past helicopter rides. Review Title: This review is a long time coming! (visited 9/2010)
Review Text:
So, let me begin by saying that our trip to Hawaii was over a year ago (September 3-11, 2010), and I should have written this review a long time ago. I was 6 months pregnant when I went to Hawaii, and "pregnancy brain" was really getting to me, so it took me this long to get my mind back. (Well, not really, it's still gone considering I have a 9 month old!).
We started to plan our trip to Hawaii in March 2010, and actually didn't even think we could have children at the time! Then, lo and behold, found out I was pregant in April 2010. Many aspects of our trip had to change as a result. We could not do the cruise we had booked, because I would be too far along for them to let me sail. And we had a catamaran tour planned, that also suggested I not take their tour.
But we still wanted to see the beauty of Kauai!
My husband found Wings Over Kauai, and we read reviews and decided this would be a great way to see it!
I am SO happy we took this tour!
Unfortunately, the first day we tried to go it started pouring down rain and rained for hours. Bruce's main concern was our safety and enjoyment, so he suggested we come back the next day. There was no way we could have seen anything from the plane because of the clouds. We noticed that the helicoptors were still doing their tours, despite the bad weather. I would imagine those tourists were disappointed!
But luckily, we had a professional like Bruce who actually cared more about his customers having a wonderful time, and also about their safety, than money.
So we came back the next day, and it was definitely worth the wait!
We took the larger plane. My husband is 6'10", so he never would have fit in the smaller plane. He sat in the very back so he would have leg room. There was one other couple with us.
I can't say enough about how much we enjoyed this tour. Bruce was so friendly, and knew everything about Kauai, and all the different plants. He taught us so much. We loved his commentary along the way.
He had great suggestions for dealing with motion sickness. He also had water and mints to help if we did get motion sick. Neither my husband nor I had ever had a problem with this, but I must say, near the end of the trip, my husband was white as a sheet, and I wasn't feeling so great myself, lol. If it hadn't been for Bruce's suggestions, it could have been a lot worse!
The tour was BEAUTIFUL, and words just can't describe it. It was definitely one of the highlights of our trip. The absolute best thing about it was the people. Bruce is terrific, and the lady helping him, Marin, was so friendly and helpful.
We will always remember our trip to Hawaii. It was my dream come true to go there, and this tour made it even more special!

Review Title: You can't find nicer people to do business with!
Review Text:
Often one reads or hears great reviews and then can't help but be let down. Such was not the case with Wings Over Kauai unless you count being let down gently at the end of the flight. Before the flight, we were sent a map showing us how to walk from where our ship docked to the ABC store, and Ellen (one of the owners of the business) promptly picked us up at 9 AM in a nice van so all six of us in our group could travel to the airport together.

Our pilot Shaun couldn’t have been kinder. We were expecting Bruce, as we didn't realize the company had two pilots and had only read about Bruce, but Shaun was very competent and cordial and welcomed questions and also was cool about others pointing out nearby planes or helicopters, which is important for a pilot to be good about making people feel free to do.

Ellen also couldn't have been kinder. She gave me a kakua nut necklace for booking the trip (at least one woman from another plane tour booked by our group also got a lei) and gave all the females flowers for their hair, and took our photo by the plane and had that as a cover to a DVD on the highlights of their tour, which she gave for free to each party in our party of six who didn’t live with another party member (which meant 4 DVDs for our group!). She also supplied a ginger candy to each passenger to help with motion sickness in case anyone was susceptible to that (none in out plane were, but in one of our other two groups to go up, I think two or three were), and also gave us free waters.

The sights on this tour were amazing and made us feel like we need not bother driving to Waimea Canyon, so we scratched that from what to do after the tour and headed to Hanalei at Shaun's suggestion. Shaun doubled back over some spots to be sure people on both sides of the plane got to view things like a blow hole. The only drawback I saw of this tour was that the plane can’t dip into places like a helicopter can, so keep that in mind if you really want to get down into places (up close to falls and such). But also keep in mind that the Wings Over Kauai flight is far less expensive than a helicopter ride (it’s $520 with tax for a plane, so if you have only 4 people, it’s $130 with tax, but if you have six like we did, it was only $86.67/person, and the helicopter on Kauai will likely run you over $210/person) and the people simply couldn’t have been nicer, so I was pleased to do business with them.

Maren, their office worker, is also sweet as molasses and a pleasure to correspond with both via email and phone; she was also quite cute in making a typo and writing "vowel renewal ceremony" in an email, which resulted in my husband and I starting off our 25th anniversary vow renewal ceremony with a joke about how our ceremony was not a vowel renewal, even with how almost half the Hawaiian alphabet is comprised of vowels, as it's not about I or U, but about Aaaa and Eee and sometimes "WHY?" And I forgot "Oh" there, and oh, I also forgot that Ellen also allowed us to get a photo behind her counter at the airport (so we could pretend we were airport personnel and say, "May I have your boarding pass, please?") and once she got our second group of people up in the air, dropped us off at Alamo for us to pick up our rental. She also let us sit on the plane where we wished (though she will need to weigh each of you, she won't tell you your weight if you don't want to know) - we just had to make out a diagram showing where we each should be. Blue Hawaii Helicopters decide for people where they will sit. Another oh...Ellen also sent us our photos that she took in email with a nice thank you note. It's little touches like these which really make a business. None of the people in our group that went up on three planes in a row that day had anything but positive comments to make about the tour's views, service, etc. (just some sadly got a little motion sick, and that was not at all due to the pilot).

Review Text:
After reading other Trip Adviser reviews, we decided to take a chance on Wings Over Kauai. We were on the NCL-Pride of America 7/30 – 8/6. Ellen was great (and patient) as we swapped e-mails to work out a schedule that worked well for us and our itinerary.

We met Ellen at the designated location (ABC Store) and were quickly transported to the hangar where my wife was presented with a lei and a nice flower (a very nice touch). Paper work, a couple complementary pictures with the aircraft, a pre-flight check and we were off!

The inland area of the island was fairly overcast. Keeping safety first, Bruce did what he could to get us in the best places for the best views. As we traveled around the leeward side of the island, the clouds parted and the view of the Na Pali Coast opened up. It is hard to find words that can accurately describe the beauty of the Na Pali Coast—especially from the air. Breathtaking! The clouds started to subside as we headed inland. In one picture we can count 14 waterfalls (I’ll share it so you can see for yourself). Bruce answered every question asked of him and did a fantastic job keeping everyone engaged.

After landing, we were promptly presented with a DVD that had our picture on the cover (taken before we took off). It contained a video of the tour (previously filmed and produced to music). Ellen dropped us off at the shopping center where we met her (a short walk from the ship), but offered to take us back to the ship. We opted to grab a bottle of water at the ABC Store and walk back to the ship (with plenty of time to spare before the ship’s departure). On the walk back to the ship, I received an e-mail from Ellen that contained the pre-flight pictures (the same ones on the DVD) and a nice “thank you” note. Again, a very nice touch!

Bottom line, Captain Bruce, Ellen and Jeanne were great! Their #1 Rated Tour is not hype, it is for real! Courteous, professional, knowledgeable and safe! Treat yourself to this tour….you won’t regret it!

Review Text:
Well, there really is a reason that this is rated number 1 for attractions and activities...there really is no downside. Firstly, making a reservation by phone or online via their website is easy, painless, and Ellen replies promptly with the most polite and genuine response.
For us, on the day of our planned tour, the skies from Princeville looked gloomy and there were scattered showers, so I called Ellen because I was concerned. She immediately gave me the option to go later in the day which we chose to do, but the skies cleared beautifully anyway shortly thereafter. As an aside though, I saw several helicopters flying through rainy and gloomy skies that morning, which would have really stunk for the money they charge.
Bruce greeted us at the airport and everything ran so smoothly. The only issue is that we waited for another couple who had also reserved the flight, and they never showed, which held us up. In addition, they could have allowed someone else to reserve those seats, so if you aren't going to show, please provide common courtesy and make a simple phone call.
You will always get a window seat on this flight, and you will get to see everything there is to see in Kauai on a very comfortable, easy flight. There are fantastic photo ops, which is beneficial because the flight is slower and steady, and you are up in the air for around 70 minutes. Bruce is well informed about the island and points everything out there is to see--he's done the flight over 5,000 times.
This truly is a steal for the price, and turned out to be the highlight of our trip. Seeing the Napali coast by air turned out to be far better than by water, and having gracious, genuine hosts for our tour made it that much better...

Review Title: Flexible in accommodating the weather changes
Review Text:
If you ever consider to take a plane tour over Kauai (which you should do), this is THE company to go for. We really enjoyed their service, not only because their customized and friendly service, but also because their flexibility and consideration for the customers.

We called them on our second day morning to book the tour, as we tot the weather was pretty good then. But they said the tour was booked until 4pm, and asked if we would like to take that. I told them about my concern on the weather, they said fine, if the weather changes we can postpone it and they didn't take any deposit, which is typical for other companies.

So for the rest of that day, we kept constant contact in order to see if the weather was still good to see much, especially for the middle of the island, where the clouds usually gather, but where you can see the beautiful canyon and waterfalls. At the end, they informed us the clouds started to gather and the visibility won't be much though they can still totally do the tour around the coast. At that time, we were totally ready to go if they didn't tell us that, and we could finish the tour without much complains. But they really want us to get the most out of it, so they suggested us to wait for another day or two, since we still have time. At the end, we went on the tour on the next day morning, when we did finally see the canyon and waterfalls.

Weather condition has always been a concern to me when booking the plane/helicopter tour, but this company with their flexible service and consideration really made me feel very comfortable with it. I think at the end they just want the customers to get the best experience out of it, no matter how much money they can earn (though this kind of mindset can longer term bring much more biz).

When we arrived at the airport, we were warmly greeted by name, and treated like family from the beginning. Wings Over Kauai is a family owned business and it shows throughout the entire experience. When you walk into the airport, you become family as well.

The plane holds 6 people, but they rarely take that many up. We went up with just one other couple and the pilot, and once airborne, we all had a window seat on the right hand side -- something the helicopters can't give you. The plane is supplied with noise-canceling headsets and intercoms, and a cooler of water, soda, and even ginger candies for easily upset stomachs.

Once we were in the air, Bruce was a wealth of knowledge. He worked in agriculture (and even has a Ph.D), and is a long time island resident. He knew the history and the natural wonders of the island well and gave great explanations of the island flora.

We saw all of the sites, from the waterfalls to the Waimea Canyon to the breathtaking Napali Coast. We enjoyed every second, and Bruce's landing was the smoothest I've ever experienced. This is the one tour you can't miss on Kauai, and they even send you the photos they take afterwards via email -- free of charge.

I am indeed more impressed with Wings Over Kauai than I expected, and I hope that anyone visiting Kaua'i will give it an even chance when weighing their options to see the island by air.

My partner and I had brought my parents to Kauai to celebrate their 50th anniversary. Our original plans had been to view the Na Pali coast from a catamaran snorkel cruise, but the high surf during our visit canceled that. Even though Jay and I had been to Kauai on 3 previous visits, we'd never seen it from the air. So I took a chance and booked a personalized flight with Bruce for our last full day on the island.

In the end, this 70 minute flight allowed us to see so much more than the snorkel cruise would have and it even cost less. We shot so many pictures that it I'm still going through them and continuing to be surprised at what we saw. With the high-quality headsets on the plane, we were all able to talk to each other and everyone had the same view of what we were seeing since we were all on the right side of the plane.

If I had it do over again, the only thing I'd do differently is that I'd take this flight at the beginning of my trip so that we could visit some of the places that we saw from above but which I would not have otherwise known even existed.

Review Text:
Our flight with Wings over Kauai last week was a highlight of our vacation. The hundreds of positive reviews here on Trip Advisor don't lie: this is an excellent way to see all the beauty of Kauai.

I'm a bit of a nervous flyer and often have motion sickness. The Wings Over Kauai staff calmed my fears and helped us prepare for a great flight. The flight (we were in the larger plane, but it was just my husband & I) was very smooth taking off and landing. The staff let me know there might be some slight bumps as we moved from the Waimea Canyon area to the coast, but even that section was really smooth. They had a cooler with drinks and cold cloths to calm down motion sickness, but we didn't need either.

Captain Bruce was incredibly well-informed about Kauai: geography, history, geology, agriculture, movies, celebrities, beaches, hotels... you name it, he knows about it, and offers great explanations of what you're seeing and answers any questions you have. Unlike a few other people I interacted with on the trip, Wings Over Kauai's staff always gave accurate and appropriate answers. Bruce was also friendly. Some of it was certainly the same lines he gives every tour, but he was very open to answering our questions, and always called us by name (a nice touch).

Could you see the same things in a helicopter? Yes, I think you could. But, Wings Over Kauai offers a similar tour, at about half the cost, and without nearly as much motion-sickness potential. (All my friends who had visited Kauai told horror stories of being sick on helicopters; none of that with Wings Over Kauai). And, though they do weigh you (it's done discreetly) the weight limit isn't nearly as much of a concern as on a helicopter.

I can see why Wings Over Kauai receives such positive reviews! With so many parts of Kauai only visible from the air, you want to take a tour, and Wings Over Kauai is a most excellent way to do that.

Review Title: Wings Over Kauai is a fantastic excursion!
Review Text:
My husband and I decided to book a tour with Wings Over Kauai after reading all the positive reviews on Trip Advisor about this service. We were not disappointed! After all the activities we did on our honeymoon this flight tour remains my husband's favorite part of the trip.

Upon showing up to the Lihue Airport for check-in, we were greeted by friendly faces. Ellen (the pilot's wife) gave me a very nice lei and Hawaiian flower for my hair to welcome us. We then went over safety information, were given tips on how to avoid motion sickness in the small craft, and also tips on how to take great pictures in flight.

Before getting into the plane we had our picture taken with the aircraft that Ellen then emailed us before we were even done with our tour! We met with Bruce, the pilot, to discuss weather conditions and where our tour would be going and then we hopped in the plane.

For someone who has never been in such a small aircraft I was a little nervous about flying but this uneasiness quickly disappeared when we took off without jolt or bump. Once in the air we were treated to a great narrative by Bruce who has his PhD in agriculture and has lived on the island for over 15 years. We saw the beautiful southern beaches, flew over Waimea Canyon, continued around to the Na'pali Coast, and around Hanalei Bay before returning to the airport. We were also lucky enough to see many waterfalls deep in the mountains and get great pictures of Wailua Falls with the sun shining right on it.

Overall, a great experience with a skilled pilot. The excellent and friendly customer service (complete with free DVD with your picture on the cover) was great bonus. The price of the flight was well worth it and we both highly recommend you join Bruce on his next flight with Wings of Kauai!

Review Title: The NICEST, SAFEST, MOST AMAZING way to see Kauai!
Review Text:
Everyone at Wings Over Kauai are absolutely wonderful! My husband and I were greeted at their office at the airport with smiles and congrats (we were on our honeymoon) and treated like family immediately! It was an unbelievably personal experience. You can really tell that these people care about their services, their customers and the experience they are providing. They seem to follow the motto "Treat others how you would like to be treated".
First off, they took pictures of my husband and I in front of the plane and with Bruce, the pilot, and emailed them to us immediately. They also gave us a DVD of the tour (not the exact tour we took, but a video of one just like it). And they did this all for FREE! My husband and I were expecting to be asked if we would like to buy the pictures they took at the end of the tour (like they do at amusement parks and stuff) but we were totally shocked when they just emailed them right away. It was a really, nice unexpected perk.
Second, everyone we dealt with was so accommodating and friendly. We received great instructions on everything and felt really tended to. This is what a Mom and Pop operation is all about!
Third, Bruce is a very, very good pilot. My husband was very nervous about going up in a plane that small but the ride was smoother than the rides we took on the jumbo jets to get to Hawaii. There was never a moment -from take off to landing - where I had any bit of nerves or felt unsafe. Bruce really knows what he's doing.
Fourth, Bruce is very knowledgeable of the island. He has a Ph.D. in agriculture-something or other and was able to tell us all about the environment on Kauai, which made the tour way better!
Overall, DO THIS TOUR!!! I saw the helicopters and they were loud, wobbley and unsafe looking. This private tour - it was just me, my husband and Bruce - is THE ONLY WAY to see Kauai. You can focus on all the beauty and not be worried about safety, other people, or an uptight "commercial" tour company.
All the things you are looking for in a tour are here - great price, extremely safe, WONDERFUL customer service! I took over 100 pictures in the plane because it was THAT GREAT!!

Review Title: Impeccable service and what a view from the air
Review Text:
We chose WOK over helicopter tours because (1) the reviews here (2) able to request a private flight for my family of 4 on GA-8 Airvan (3) everyone get window seat (4) the significant cost saving. Our objectives were met 100%.

Based on the reviews here, we decided to go on WOK as early as we could. However, it was cloudy on our first morning in Kauai. Since this was our first trip to Kauai, I didn’t know whether that was weather as usual (since it often rains in Kauai) or just a cloudy day. We arrived at the airport on time. Ellen’s first reaction was “you didn’t get my message”. Guess what, Ellen had called to suggest flying on other time. The cloud cleared up in the afternoon. I called again to check with Ellen. Ellen suggested if we went on the afternoon flight, we won’t get the flight for my own and the children would need to sit on the left side of the plane since she had rearranged other morning flight passengers to afternoon already. To make the long story short, Ellen keeps customer’s best interest in mind. That’s something very commendable.

We finally got on the flight on our last day. It was a beautiful day with blue sky. Kauai is as advertised as beautiful from the sky. You truly need to take a flight to see the mountain, valley, waterfalls and coastline. Since we had been to a few places already in Kauai, able to recognize places like Wailua Fall in the air was fun.

We all felt dizzy to different degree in the flight. The flight was smooth so it’s more due to our physical condition than anything else. Another thing, my video and pictures captured quite a bit of cockpit reflection. If you plan to take a lot of pictures and videos, beware of the reflection or don’t sit on the right co-pilot seat. The complementary DVD with our photo on the cover made up some from the glare. A follow up email is also a nice touch. WOK does not need to do any of these, but they do!

Overall, it is a wonderful experience and I will suggest taking this flight to anyone else.

Review Text:
For our 25th wedding anniversary, we really wanted to book a helicopter tour of Kauai. Steve and Lori from Tom Barefoot Tours TomBarefoot.com highly recommended booking a fixed wing flight on a Cessna from Wings Over Kauai. We're glad we took their advice. We flew with Wings Over Kaui on Thursday, July 15, 2010.

It's a true "mom and pop" operation run by Ellen and Bruce Coulombe. Both are very friendly, warm and accommodating. Ellen picked us up in town (we were on the NCL cruise ship Pride of America) and drove us to the airport. Flight check in was very smooth. She answered all our questions, even giving my wife a welcome gift and taking our photos in front of the Cessna.

My wife Maria was a bit hesitant to fly in a small 4 seat airplane. She told Bruce our pilot that she might feel queasy. Bruce put both of at ease with his wonderful suggestions for avoiding motion sickness. He also had on hand some ginger candies which his lovely wife Ellen told us were very effective in settling any upset stomachs.

Maria sat up in front, while I had the back all to myself. One great advantage of a fixed wing airplane is that you're guaranteed a window seat! Maria helped Bruce with the pre flight checklist.

This is a great way to see the island since you can't see it by car. Bruce pointed out all the must see sights and giving us his personal anecdotes as well. Bruce has a great sense of humour, a wealth of information and knowledge of Kauai, (he has a PhD in agronomy) and a masterful way of telling great stories.

It went by way too fast! This was a real personal tour. We highly recommend Wings Over Kauai for their unbeatable prices, longer flight time, and pickup and return if you're on a cruise or without a car.

Review Title: Wonderful flight with a top notch company
Review Text:
Ellen and Bruce, the owners of Wings over Kauai are two of the nicest people that you’ll ever meet. The reservation process with Ellen was smooth and enjoyable and she is very personable.

We had received a phone call from Ellen yesterday letting us know that they had an unexpected inspection of their larger plane (GA-8 Airvan) scheduled for today so we wouldn’t all be able to fly together on our scheduled sightseeing flight. She had offered us the option to take two separate flights on their smaller aircraft (Cessna 172) or to take their competitor Air Venture (she had even talked to Air Venture about available flight times with them). We decided to stick with Wings over Kauai and were glad we did.

We decided that my step son and I would take the first flight at 11 am and that my wife and step daughter would take the later flight at 12:30 pm. Ellen picked us up at the ABC store near the ship (it’s about a 10 minute walk or a free shuttle ride) and we headed to the airport where we weighed in and waited until Bruce was ready. I sat up front with Bruce and my step son sat in the back. The Cessna was definitely small and was by far the smallest aircraft that I’ve ever been in, and I was a bit nervous at first. Bruce’s calm manner and professionalism quickly put me at ease though. We both had on headphones so we could hear Bruce’s narration and converse with him. As we taxied out, he had me read off his preflight check list which was fun. He is very methodical and safety conscious so I felt like we were in very good hands. Soon we were cleared for takeoff and it didn’t take long for us to be airborne. We flew over Waimea Canyon, the Na Pali coast, the waterfall from Fantasy Island, and even saw the summit of Mount Waialeale which Bruce said was rare (it’s one of the rainiest spots on earth with an average of 426 inches of rain per year). We saw numerous mountains, waterfalls, beaches, and beautiful coastline on our flight and Bruce is a veritable encyclopedia of knowledge. I haven’t done any helicopter flights but couldn’t imagine it being any better than this, and at a much cheaper price than a helicopter too. We flew over the Pride of America on our way back to the airport and all too soon were coming in for a smooth, smooth landing.

My wife and step daughter were waiting at the airport for their flight so Ellen took a picture of all four of us in front of the plane. That picture ended up on the cover of the free dvd that they gave us (which features footage from what we saw on the flight but not from our specific flight). Ellen drove us back to the ABC store (she offered to take us to the ship but we wanted to buy a few t-shirts) and bid us a fond farewell. Later, when my wife returned, her and my step daughter raved about their flight and we all compared notes. What a wonderful experience.

Review Title: The best way to see Kauai "Wings Over Kauai"!
Review Text: Our son took us to Kauai for vacation and when he checked out the ratings on Trip Advisor for an aerial tour we took note of the highly recommended and great reviews for Wings Over Kauai. This was a great decision as there were 5 in our group, so I booked the AirVan which can carry 6 people instead of the Cessna so that we could all ride together.   One of the members of our group was a bit  apprehensive to take the tour with us, but she did anyway and survived the wonderful trip without losing it.   Upon arrival at WOK, Bruce graciously greeted us and shortly there after Ellen warmly welcomed us, too.   She presented me with a Kukui Nut necklace and a small flower, too.  They were so hospitable and treated us like family which made our Katie feel so much better about joining us on the tour.  We took the tour at 12:30 pm and had beautiful weather for our flight.  Bruce assisted us with taking our picture in front of the Air Van before our takeoff.   We had bottled drinks available and some ginger candy to assist us with flight sickness if we needed it.  Then he helped us strap in and showed us how to use the headsets.  They allowed us to converse with him and ask questions during the flight which was really neat.  Bruce was our pilot and our son, Jeff was his co-pilot and had the job of assisting Bruce with the pre-flight checklist as we made our way down the run way.  We chartered the whole plane for our group of 5 and paid a total of $520 including tax since it was less expensive that paying the $130 per person + tax for the flight.   What a deal!  Our view of the Waimea Canyon, the Na Pali Coast, Wailua Falls and many other breathtaking sights was just awesome.   I took about 150 pictures and the majority of them came out great!  We highly recommend using Wings Over Kauai for your aerial view of the island.   Mahalo,  Ellen and Bruce for a wonderful adventure!

Review Text:
This is not just a review of the Wings Over Kauai marvelous circle island flight, but also about the aloha of their family, Bruce, Ellen and daughter Mary.

Reservations were easy, happy and fun, when I talked with Ellen, to reserve two seats for us. We talked story, and just had a ball. Ellen is so full of life and aloha, and infectious happy laughter makes a person feel like you are talking to a long time friend.

On the day we were sheduled, Ellen calls and reminds us of the flight, and says everything is a " go". She also says that she will not be there, but her daughter Mary will be running the office.

Kidding around, I say " Well , just how am I going to give you an aloha hug ? " Ellen replys " Give the hug to my daughter, and she can pass it on ! " How cool is that. I love this island and the people.

We are excited about flying in their brand new G-8 Aerovan. That puppy has room for 6, but generally they just fly four. Huge windows for photo opportunities, and plenty of leg room. Seats run along each side seperated by an isle in the center.

Each passenger has a headseat and mic, and Bruce , the owner, and pilot, visits and talks with each individual, calling them by their first names. The naration of the flight is excellent, as Bruce has years and years of experience flying the tour in his Cessna 172, plus he has many, many years as a resident on Kauai. Knows his stuff.

Prior to departure we weigh in and sign in....Mary escorts us out to the G-8, to the ladder leading into the main cabin. She will take pre boarding photos with your camera , as well as hers.

Also the ladies all receive a kukui nut lei...which I placed over Erica's shoulders and gave her the traditional kiss. The fun had already begun and we were still on the ground.

Take off was smooth, and I rode up in the right seat, ( co-pilot seat ) next to Bruce. Not sure if it makes any difference, but I was a professional pilot for nearly 40 years. No stick time in the G-8, but it was great fun helping read off the check list, and feeling a bit like part of the aircrew.

Take off was smooth and we gently banked to the right, and began our climb out for the Circle Island Tour. The passengers in the back had their cameras ready.

Bruce flys slow and at an altitude that is superb for photos as we were treated to marvelous panoramic views of the garden island. Seems like we fly about the same routes as the helo companies, with thoughtful attention to noise abatement in certain areas.

Roughly, we cruised past Kalapaki Beach, and Nawiliwili Harbor. On our right the cameras clicked with shots of Kipu Kai, Maha'ulepu, The Hyatt and Poipu. Turning inland we crossed over the coffee fields of Kalaheo, and then to some of the canyons in the Hanapepe Valley.

Wonderful vistas of Waimea Canyon opened up, and then flew over the ridge and waimea canyon road, and the deep valleys that lead to the Napali Coast. Soon we were cruising along the Napali Coast . Banking inland about Hanalei, the interior beauty, lush valleys, water falls and rivers were marvelous. More natural tresures passed beneath us, as we circled Wialua Falls.....

That is just part of the flying experience, you will be seeing much more, and even though we live on Kauai, learned all kinds of new information about the island.

Flight time is nearly up, and we fly very near our condo, at Banyon Harbor, which is on the approach to runway 3.

We have a cross wind, and Bruce landed so sofly that I could not feel the wheel touch down. Maybe jus a slight kiss as he rolled it on. I kidded him " You had better call the tower and confirm that we are on the ground ! " Bruce just smiled.

Now remember when Mary took photos of both couples prior to departure. Well, we taxi up to the Commuter Terminal and shut down. Mary brings out the steps for easy exiting of the aircraft.

Everyone is happy and smiling, Mary presents us with WOK's professional DVD of the route of flight. Back ground music is by IZ. And, on the front of the DVD plastic holder is the picture of each individual couple. Yep, Erica and I are pictured just below the WINGS OVER KAUAI name on the top.

Will just finish by saying that the G-8, is a product of Australia, and flown as a tour aircraft down under. It can haul the weight. Which, is great for those who weigh more than the max limit to fly a helo tour without purchasing an extra seat, or a percentage of an extra seat.

No extra charge. There is plenty of leg and shoulder room, and I belive the cost is about $ 249.00 for two people. That is pretty reasonable and about half the cost of some of the helo tours give or take a few bucks. Not bad !

We looked out our DVD this morning, now this is professionally done. It is not a dvd of our particular flight, and is outstanding. Perfect for showing friends and family upon returning to your home base. And it is also included. No extra charge.

The Wings Over Kauai cirdle island tour, was most outstanding. Bruce, Ellen and Mary were wonderful, and make each individual passenger feel like they are the only people that exist on the planet. Lots of individual customer service and aloha.

Denny and Erica
Lihue, Hawaii

Review Title: If you do only one thing on Kaua'i, do Wings Over Kaua'i
Review Text:
Wings Over Kaua'i has 320 reviews on TripAdvisor. Of those, well over 300 were 5 stars, the rest four. Any time an attraction manages to please everybody, they're doing something right.

The 70 minute Grand Tour is perfect for anyone daytripping from another island, and if you have only time for one thing on Kaua'i this should be it. Pilot Dr. Bruce Columbe and his charming wife run the show, and all their efforts are devoted to safety first, then a superb experience for their passengers.

The plane has all passenger seats on the right side, so everyone gets a window view of the clockwise tour. Noise-cancelling headphones with microphones enable all to hear the pilot's narration (amusing and informative) and to ask questions or make comments to all.

And what a tour! Kaua'i is among the most beautiful places on the planet, and the aerial views of the Na Pali Coast, Waimea Canyon, and the extinct volcano at the center of the island, the wettest spot on earth with waterfalls everywhere, were breathtaking!

Fixed-wing tours are less than half the cost of helicopter tours, and use less than half the fuel. For reasons I can't explain, Fodor's guide doesn't even mention their existence (though I did send an email to the Hawai'i editor to amend future editions). This was the highlight of our trip (that included Big Island), and the competition for that title was quite intense.

Review Text:
Bruce, Ellen, and Thomas were all very friendly and helpful. Bruce did his best to avoid bumpy air the day we flew, but alas, my travel companion still got a little queezy (she used wrist bands, but no other medication, for motion sickness). The views were gorgeous; I just wish we'd been able to fly over Waimea Canyon instead of near it (didn't see much of it), but the bumpy air prevented our doing so.

Bruce is very knowledgeable about the island, which made the flight educational. I would also have liked him to give more of a running narrative of the names of the areas, beaches, towns, etc. that we were flying over along the way to provide a better orientation to the island. We took the flight on the first day of our stay; it would be helpful to know the names of the places we saw so we could find them to explore from the ground later.

All in all, flying with WOK is a great value and I'd recommend it to anyone.

Review Title: Why would you want to take a helicopter???
Review Text:
It appears that the key choice in chosing an air tour is to go by helicopter or by airplane. The hotels always seem to recommend the helicopter tour, but why? Could it be that they just recommend the most expensive option? Take the airplane! It's half the cost, and you see the same places.

Captain Bruce of Wings of Kauai has been flying for years, and his skill sets proved it to me. As a commercial pilot myself, I notice things that most people don't. I VALUE SAFETY ABOVE ALL ELSE. Case in point. There was another aircraft within sight that decided to fly up a canyon, one where the clouds were very low. As I sat in the seat, I wondered if our captain was going to follow him. My concern was that the clouds were too low to remain legally VFR (visual flight reference), a standard that tour planes must adhere to for safety sake because no IFR (Instrument Flight Rules) plan had been filed. Flying into or too close to those clouds can spell trouble, after all, where are the sides of the canyon if you can't see them? Draw your own conclusions.

Captain Bruce made a consciencous decision to take a different route, and we saw the same sights. Later I asked him why he took that route, and he replied, "Safety comes first, and I did not want to risk my passengers". There is a saying in aviation: There are old pilots and there are bold pilots, but there are no old, bold pilots. I appreciated his decision and concern for safety rather than take a risk just we could see the same sight from a different perspective.

There are two rows of seats in the aircraft. He only books the seats on the right hand side of the aircraft so everyone gets a window seat. Great for visuals and great for photos. Would you get that treatment in a crowded helicopter?

We actually flew through a double rainbow that totally engulfed the aircraft. I've never seen anything like it. I totally encircled the aircraft. It was above us, beside us and below us. I've never experienced anything like it before.

In any case, I give Wings over Kauai a five star rating. Great people. Great trip. Great memories. Great photos.

Review Title: We felt safe and well take care of before, during, & after the flight.
Review Text: My wife and I had the pleasure of taking a flight with Bruce and Wings Over Kauai on February 8, 2010. Review Text:
We took a Cruise around Hawaii in October 09 and as an excursion on 30 October did a tour over Kauai with Wings Over Kauai.
I had been so impressed with the service I received before even stepping foot on the plane to come to Hawaii - months before we had had e-mail correspondence and received fast responses to every question and query.
On the morning of the flight, an employee was sent to pick us up from near where our Cruise ship was docked to take us to the airfield. Ellen (and their cute dog!!) greeted us at the office, answered all our questions and even offered me some ginger root, remembering that I had told her before that i suffered from motion sickness.
As it turned out, I didn't need anything, as the flight was so smooth, and I was relaxed even more by the fact that Bruce told us we could open the window if either of us started to feel sick.
I can honestly say that we saw some of the most beautiful sights I have ever seen on that hour tour, and it was so useful to have Bruce's commentary so we actually knew what we were looking at!
I would recommend Wings Over Kauai to anyone visiting Kauai, even if just there for a couple of days (as we were!) - there was absolutely nothing that could have been improved!

Review Text:
The highlight of our trip to Kauai was the personal touch both on the ground by Ellen and in the air with Bruce.

The review of Safety items, the care with which the clients were boarded and the instructions both on the ground and in the air were well done.
We were made to feel special and every effort was being made to ensure that all the bases were covered and still enjoy the flight and the spectacular scenery.

I understand that there have been some complaints by home owners of aircraft overflights. Our flight was high and an effort was made to be unobtrusive. Perhaps if I owned a condo or home, I would find the noise of aircraft intrusive at times, but there is a place for organized aerial touring, done in a safe and efficient manner with consideration for the home owner.
We could not have seen or discovered in a week on the ground, all of the wonderful terrain features or animal life that we were were able to see in a one hour flight with personal narration and response to questions by Bruce.

Whether to go by airplane or helicopter was a difficult choice. I am a helicopter pilot with more than 19000 hours of helicopter flight time. I know the capabilities of the helicopter and they are awesome.
We chose to go by airplane because we wanted to have a less expensive choice. This was at the end of a 19 day vacation at the end of my second retirement. With the zoom capability of my movie camera, getting up close and personal was not a requirement.
The airplane met or exceeded all of our requirements.

Our visit for my wife and I, to Kauai was wonderful.
Thank you Bruce and Ellen Coulombe.

Bob and Sandy

Review Title: 90% the helicopter experience, and 50% the price.
Review Text: I'm a private pilot with some 1300 hours in a Cessna 172 and with a perhaps silly desire to log a landing in all 50 states. (I'm up to 37 as of yesterday.) Having already experienced a helicopter tour of Na Pali and Waimea Canyon, and having also (two years ago) kayaked Na Pali, all I really wanted was to fly once or twice around the airport and get a landing or two. That said, I decided instead to hire Bruce to give me one-hour flight training as I flew from the left seat as he guided me and my wife (in back seat) on their usual one hour tour. I'm so glad I did! Not only is Bruce a great narrator and knowledgable, but he is a confidence inspiring instructor, a smooth pilot, and the view from the Skyhawk, while not quite as up-close as what you'd get in a helicopter, is outstanding. Highly recommended. And the Bose noise-cancelling headsets work great, almost as well as my Zulu's.  :)

Review Text:

Our table mates at Laua Kalamaku told us that their helicopter tour was terrifying. The wife's seatbeat came unbuckled halfway through the air-tour, and there are no doors on the helicopter. She had to hang on for dear life as her husband tried to get her seat belt-style buckle back on. And there were no noise-canceling headphones, so it was super loud.

Well, given all that, we chose Wings over Kauai and could not have been happier. The plane was very steady and safe feeling. Each passenger gets noise-cancelling bose headsets, and the pilot gives a lovely tour with hawaiian music in the headset if you like. The scenery is absolutely stunning and we couldn't have felt safer!

Check them out at www.wingsoverkauai.com

Review Text: After reading the reviews on trip advisor, we chose to go on a tour with Wings Over Kauai.  Everything promised from all the previous reviews proved true. I would actually pay higher than the going rate for this tour of the island because of Bruce (the pilot) being so knowledgable about the island. Review Text:
I called Wings Over Kauai to book a flight for my birthday, and I cannot say enough great things about this company. I spoke with Ellen on the phone a couple of times and she was so sweet and helpful in booking our flight. When we arrived, we were greeted by the pilot, Bruce, who wished me a happy birthday, chatted with us a bit, collected our payment, went through a short information and safety briefing, and then took us up on the flight of a lifetime!

Capt. Review Text:
We decided to take this flight whilst calling at the island on a Princess Cruises tour of the Hawaian Islands. Whilst considering our shore excursions before leaving England we knew that we wanted to see Kauai from the air, but should we choose a Helicopter or a Plane? Princess wanted US$269 each for a 55 minute shared helicopter flight including ground transport; WoK charged us US$249 FOR THE TWO OF US including 'trimmings' (see below) with exclusive use of the plane and ground transport. They also confirmed that if, for some reason, the ship could not dock we would not be charged. Always one for a bargain, I booked - but was it any good?

It was arranged that Ellen would meet us at a shopping centre close to the ship at 10.30am for our 11.00am flight for a private car transfer to the airport - but she was late!! I have never known anyone so apologetic about being 3 minutes late (try waiting for a local train in the UK Ellen, they don't even call it late in their performance statistics unless it is 5 minutes late and they don't even apologise if it is 13 minutes late).

After our transfer to the airport during which Ellen told us all about Bruce and her backgrounds we carried out the paperwork (and weighing!) with Ellen whilst Bruce prepared the plane. My wife was presented with a flower for her hair and a nut lei to wear and we proceeded to the plane, having our photo taken alongside it.

My wife, having a slightly more petite build than me (!), was chosen as being the best person for the front seat with me having room to spread out in the back. She helped Bruce with his pre-flight checks and we were then away. The in-flight refreshments were not used by us - we were too interested in the scenery.

We had been warned to wear a dark top (to prevent reflections in the windows) and as a result of this I did not need to open windows to take my numerous photographs.

Was it a good decision to take a plane rather than a helicopter? As the saying goes 'you pays your money, you takes your choice'. Of necessity, the place operates at a higher level than the helicopter and cannot go deep into the valleys; however, for a lot of our flight I could see a helicopter operating beneath us. It appeared very close to the ground and I cannot believe that it could have provided as good a photo as some of those taken by me on my rather basic camera. Ours was also very much a personalised trip whereas a helicopter would have been shared, following a pre-determined route.

We were able to fly over our ship to take pictures from the air and also more unusual sights such as the massive Costco and Car Park from the air.

As we returned to the airport it was an interesting experience to land on one runway at the same time as a 'proper' passenger plane was landing on the main runway. Like others, we were presented with a DVD with our own pictures on the front.

We were intending going on afterwards to the Kilohana Plantation which we thought was close-by but was actually a fair distance away. Ellen offered to take us as she was heading in that direction. She needn't have done this, however, it was typical of Ellen and Bruce. Their main concern was to ensure that we had a great day, which we did.

If you book with WoK you will not be sorry. Enjoy the experience; we certainly did.

Review Text:

Bruce and Ellen's late model Cessna 172S is spacious and clean. What I appreciated most was how stable the aircraft flys around the beautiful mountain palis. And with it's high wing configuration, you get to see everything around and below you. My wife took over 100 photos during our 70 minute adventure.

After circling the island and flying over Wiama Canyon, we contacted the Lihue tower for a clearance to land. The entire experience was excellent, providing an up close view of areas otherwise inaccessible. As a private pilot, it was a real thrill for me to land the aircraft on the same island runway that the large commercial jets, including the one we had flown in used. Whether you're a pilot, or you let Captain Bruce do all the flying for you, I'd recommend Wings Over Hawaii...for anyone wanting a safe, slow ride around the Garden Isle!
